_meta.note: Every threshold carries its own `source`, exactly as parts.py does. An uncited threshold is an invented number wearing a lab coat, and dfm.load_rules refuses to load one. Keys are unit-suffixed (_mm, _deg, _mm2) because JSON cannot carry the convention that a bare number is millimetres. `compare` says which side of the value is a violation: `min` means the measured number must be at least the value, `max` means at most.
_meta.severities: BLOCKER stops a print; WARNING is worth reading before committing six hours; NOTE is informational. Only BLOCKER is intended to gate, and only where an intent.json asserts on it (ADR-8).

min_feature_mm.source: a feature thinner than one bead does not print

min_hole_d_mm.source: FDM bores below 2mm close up from arc faceting and flow

max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, measured from vertical

min_footprint_mm2.source: bed adhesion / tipping risk on a tall part

max_aspect_ratio.source: height divided by the smaller footprint dimension

PLA_generic._note: PLA is the permissive case; it holds the defaults verbatim so the comparison against the other two materials is explicit rather than implied by absence.

max_overhang_deg.note: PLA solidifies fast enough to hold the conventional threshold
max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, measured from vertical

PETG_generic._note: PETG stays soft longer than PLA and strings; overhangs droop and long bridges sag before they set.

max_overhang_deg.note: PETG's longer melt tail droops where PLA would hold
max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, tightened 5 deg for PETG

max_bridge_mm.note: half the PLA span; PETG bridges sag rather than snapping taut
max_bridge_mm.source: unsupported bridge span before sag, halved for PETG

ABS_generic._note: ABS shrinks on cooling. The overhang and bridge numbers tighten for the same reason PETG's do, and the footprint minimum rises because warping lifts a small footprint off the plate.

max_overhang_deg.note: cooling shrinkage curls an unsupported edge upward into the nozzle
max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, tightened 5 deg for ABS

max_bridge_mm.source: unsupported bridge span before sag, tightened for ABS

min_footprint_mm2.note: ABS warps; a small footprint lifts a corner and the print detaches
min_footprint_mm2.source: bed adhesion / tipping risk, raised for a shrinking material

PAHT-CF_bambu._note: Bambu PAHT-CF (GFN04), the fpv frame's structural material (seanrobertwright/fpv #5). Bambu's TDS V3.0 rates it at a max overhang of ~70 deg and a max bridge of ~40 mm, which are best-case figures from Bambu's own test parts, so the overhang and bridge rules hold the conventional defaults rather than loosening to them. What does tighten is the footprint: Bambu lists 'Easy to warp' as a con, requires an enclosed printer, and 'strongly' recommends glue stick and a brim against warping. Wall and hole minimums stay at the 0.4 mm defaults; the TDS recommends a 0.6 mm nozzle and lists 0.4 mm as supported. Part cooling is 0-40% (TDS), 10-30% in Bambu's slicer profile.

max_overhang_deg.note: held at the conventional threshold; Bambu's TDS claims '~ 70 deg' under its own test conditions with 0-40% part cooling, which is not a reason to loosen a gate
max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, measured from vertical; Bambu PAHT-CF Technical Data Sheet V3.0, 'Max Overhang Angle ~ 70 deg', 'Cooling Fan 0 - 40%' (wiki.bambulab.com/filament-acc/asacf-pahtcf/65f1b18a6d6142d794a1a6a00f1496ef.pdf, read 2026-10-07)

max_bridge_mm.note: held at the default; Bambu's TDS claims '~ 40 mm', four times this, as a best case
max_bridge_mm.source: unsupported bridge span before sag; Bambu PAHT-CF Technical Data Sheet V3.0, 'Max Bridging Length ~ 40 mm' (read 2026-10-07)

min_footprint_mm2.note: nylon warps as it cools and a small footprint lifts a corner off the plate; Bambu requires an enclosure and recommends glue stick plus a brim for exactly this
min_footprint_mm2.source: bed adhesion / tipping risk, raised for a warping material, as for ABS; bambulab.com/en/filament/paht-cf lists 'Easy to warp' under Cons and 'Enclosure Printer Required'; wiki.bambulab.com/en/filament/asacf_pahtcf: 'To minimize warping, it is strongly recommended to ... apply Bambu Lab Glue Stick' and 'Enable a Brim' (read 2026-10-07)

TPU-95A_bambu._note: Bambu TPU 95A (GFU01), the fpv frame's soft material for bumpers, clips and cradles (seanrobertwright/fpv #5). Bambu's TDS V2.0 rates it at a max overhang of ~70 deg, the same as PAHT-CF, with 100% part cooling, so the overhang rule holds the default. Its max bridging length is 20 mm against PAHT-CF's ~40 mm, so the bridge rule is halved in the same ratio: a soft bead stretched across a gap sags under its own weight. Bambu's wiki says TPU 95A is not AMS-compatible (too soft for the feed channel), so it runs from the external spool.

max_overhang_deg.note: held at the conventional threshold; TDS claims '~70 deg' with 'Cooling Fan 100%'
max_overhang_deg.source: conventional FDM support threshold, measured from vertical; Bambu TPU 95A Technical Data Sheet V2.0, 'Max Overhang Angle ~70 deg', 'Cooling Fan 100%' (cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0584/7236/6216/files/Bambu_TPU_95A_Technical_Data_Sheet.pdf, read 2026-10-07)

max_bridge_mm.note: half the default: Bambu rates TPU 95A's bridging at half of PAHT-CF's, and a soft bead cannot be pulled taut
max_bridge_mm.source: unsupported bridge span before sag, halved for a flexible filament; Bambu TPU 95A Technical Data Sheet V2.0 'Max Bridging Length 20mm' against Bambu PAHT-CF Technical Data Sheet V3.0 'Max Bridging Length ~ 40 mm' (read 2026-10-07)
